assessment.nobel_worthiness: A new tool that opens a door: twist angle as a tuning knob for correlated and superconducting states in a van der Waals system, and the origin of the whole moire field. The 2018 correlated-insulator and superconductivity experiments are the original experiments, and the 2011 continuum-model prediction identified the magic angle. Impact on materials, devices and quantum matter is broad and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experimental discovery; Bistritzer and MacDonald made the decisive theoretical prediction. A split of experiment and theory looks fair, though I would want the historical record checked for related earlier theory and for the role of the co-first authors and group members, whose names are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many independent groups in the years since 2018, with a stable interpretation of the basic phase diagram; the microscopic pairing mechanism is still debated, but the discovery itself is solid and timely.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism and the nature of the correlated states remain unresolved.
I have not independently verified the details of the earlier theory literature on twisted bilayers; the supplied credit may omit relevant contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength idea, is a measurement instrument that reached fractional uncertainties around 1e-18 and opened new precision tests and geodesy applications. It is an invention with experimental verification and clear benefit.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed and first realised the magic-wavelength lattice concept; Ye's group brought the clock to the best accuracy and showed what the platform could do. Two laureates seems a clean and defensible configuration, though I would check the historical record on the roles of others working on lattice clocks and on the earlier ion-clock and frequency-comb work already honoured.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation across many laboratories and comparison of clocks; the technology is mature and in the redefinition-of-the-second discussion. Timely.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier prizes for frequency combs (2005) and ion clocks (2012) could be argued to make this an incremental step.
Other contributors to lattice clocks (for example in Europe and the US) may merit consideration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Loading ultracold atoms into optical lattices gave a controllable quantum simulator for many-body physics: the superfluid-Mott insulator transition and later single-site imaging make it possible to see strongly correlated systems directly. A genuine new window on many-body physics.
assessment.attribution: The four credited names span theory (Cirac, Zoller proposal of the Bose-Hubbard realisation with Jaksch) and experiment (Greiner et al. 2002 Mott transition, Bloch as the leading group). Attribution is unsettled: the original Mott transition experiment names, Jaksch's role and Hansch's and Kasevich's groups are not in the supplied credit. I propose one experimentalist-focused configuration but the allocation is truly open.
assessment.maturity: Replicated across many laboratories, with quantum gas microscopes now standard; very mature, though the field continues to evolve toward quantum simulation with practical impact still ahead.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should recognise the proposal, the first experiment or the quantum-gas-microscope development is unresolved.
Credit overlaps with earlier BEC and cooling prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED brought strong light-matter coupling onto a chip, underlies superconducting quantum processors and readout, and is a clear case of an invention with large downstream consequences. The 2004 Wallraff et al. experiment is the original demonstration of strong coupling.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf wrote the 2004 proposal; Wallraff and Schoelkopf carried out the experiments. Girvin is missing from the supplied credit, which makes the fair attribution harder. I would propose the experimental pair plus the lead theorist, but would want the committee to examine the record.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in many laboratories and widely used; mature. The 2025 prize for macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits is related, which may affect timing.
uncertainties: Proximity to the 2025 prize and to the earlier 2012 prize on single quantum systems may make the committee hesitate.
Credit from the supplied names omits Steven Girvin and other proposal authors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magnetic skyrmions are a topologically protected spin texture, with first observation in MnSi, real-space imaging by Lorentz TEM and spin-polarised STM, and potential for spintronic devices. Imaging tools made the objects directly visible, which I value.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is difficult: the skyrmion lattice in MnSi (neutron scattering) was led by Boni and Pfleiderer's groups; the Lorentz TEM real-space observation by Tokura's group; the atomic-scale skyrmions by Wiesendanger's group; and the theory by Bogdanov and Rossler, who are not in the supplied credit. A fair prize is hard to configure with this list.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation in many materials, but device applications are not yet realised, which weakens the benefit argument. Medium maturity.
uncertainties: Theoretical originators (Bogdanov and others) are not among the credited names.
Contributions of Muhlbauer, Yu and Heinze may be overlooked.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators opened a new class of materials with protected edge and surface states, now central to condensed-matter physics. The 2005 Kane-Mele prediction and the 2007 HgTe experiment by Molenkamp's group are the decisive discovery steps.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the original theoretical proposal; Molenkamp's group carried out the experimental confirmation based on the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang prediction. The BHZ theorists and the three-dimensional topological insulator contributors (Moore, Balents, Fu, Hasan) are not in this list, so a clean allocation is not straightforward.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed in several material systems; mature and arguably overdue, though the 2016 prize covered topological phase transitions in a different sense.
uncertainties: Missing credit for Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Fu, Moore, Hasan and others.
Possible overlap with candidate B024 on the related theme; the fair configuration is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Fractional quantum anomalous Hall states at zero field in moire materials show fractional topological order without Landau levels, a conceptually new experimental result opening the door to anyons without magnetic fields.
assessment.attribution: Several groups reported the effect in twisted MoTe2 (Xu, Mak and Shan, plus Tingxin Li and others), and a separate rhombohedral graphene result (Ju) followed. Who made the decisive original observation is contested and sensitive to dates; I would not assign credit without further record checking.
assessment.maturity: Premature: the discovery is from 2023 onward, and independent confirmation is still limited, though it is growing. Interpretation of the states is still being settled.
uncertainties: Independent confirmation and sample reproducibility remain limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first X-ray, optical and radio afterglows of gamma-ray bursts settled the extragalactic origin and distance scale of GRBs, a long-standing puzzle, from original observations in 1997. A clear discovery with large effect on high-energy astrophysics.
assessment.attribution: Costa and Frontera led the BeppoSAX detection of the X-ray afterglow, but the optical identification involved van Paradijs's team (deceased) and Kulkarni's group provided radio and redshift results; the allocation is delicate and the deceased contributor cannot be recognised.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely confirmed, perhaps long past due, which may reduce urgency, and the committee may find the 2020 and earlier astrophysics prizes sufficient.
uncertainties: Van Paradijs cannot be credited and other BeppoSAX and optical teams may be missing.
Whether the committee considers it physics rather than astronomy, given past decisions.
